context: From left to right, the figure has four sections: the “Input key” column, the “Hash function: key % 100” box, the “Index” and “Array (one key-value pair per bucket)” columns, and the “Output value” column on the far right.
The text gives the underlying array a capacity of 100. The figure uses index = key % 100, so the last two digits of the five-digit student ID give the bucket index.
description: The array shows five nonempty buckets in increasing index order. Ellipses stand for the other buckets. The table “Buckets shown in the array” lists the five entries in full. The table “Highlighted lookup paths” gives the input order, color, bucket number, and output position for each lookup.

The inputs appear in a different order from the bucket indices. The three color-coded paths cross as they pass through the calculation box, but each still connects its own input, target bucket, and output. Buckets 37 and 83 are not used in these lookups.

frames.explanation: You can verify the bucket indices in the table with the formula. For example, 13276 % 100 = 76. All three lookups compute an index, then use it to access the array.
frames.title: Three lookup paths using key % 100 to locate a bucket

summary: Compute the bucket index from the key, then read the value in that bucket.
title: A hash function maps an input key to a bucket array index
